title: A puddle can evaporate by taking heat from the sun, the air, or skin
summary: Any liquid water can evaporate, including a sidewalk puddle, when it absorbs energy from the sun, the air, or body heat.
body: NOAA Education says evaporation turns liquid water into water vapor, like moisture in the atmosphere. Any liquid water can evaporate, from falling rain to the ocean or a puddle on the sidewalk. It happens when water absorbs energy from the sun, the atmosphere, or even our own body heat. That is a wider net than a kettle on a stove. The Survey's account of bonds breaking is a different page and a different card. This one is only NOAA's list of everyday liquids and energy sources.
